Scheme in Maritime Edge Computing Network
Hongxia Zhang , Shiyu Xi , Bodong Shang , Member, IEEE, Peiying Zhang , Member, IEEE,
Sheng Wu , Member, IEEE, and Chunxiao Jiang , Fellow, IEEE
Abstract—With the development of maritime continuing to grow,
large-scale maritime wireless devices (MWDs) are being deployed
for various maritime applications. The rapid development of mar-
itime Internet of Things (IoT) and growing demand for these appli-
cations have led to an increasing number of computation-intensive
and resource-sensitive tasks. Considering the limited computing
capacity and energy of MWDs, it is challenging to transmit and
process massive maritime computing tasks in an energy efficient
manner. In this paper, we propose a three-tier maritime edge
computing system in which low earth orbit (LEO) satellite and
offshore base station (OBS) support to provide communication and
computing services for MWDs. The system optimizes association
variable, task partitioning, transmission power, and computing
resource allocation to reduce system energy consumption under
latency constraints. The optimization problem is formulated as
a mixed integer non-linear programming (MINLP) optimization
problem. We decompose the original problem into four subprob-
lems and design algorithms to solve them. Firstly, the associa-
tion variable optimization subproblem is solved by slack variable
method. Then, we adopt quadratic transformation and design a
difference of convex algorithm to solve transmission power op-
timization subproblem. Further, task partitioning subproblem is
solved by obtaining upper and lower bounds of offloading task
size by strict deduction, and then solved by the standard convex
method. Finally, Lagrangian dual method is utilized to deal with
joint computing resource optimization subproblem of LEO satellite
and OBS. In simulation results, the proposed algorithm saves
39.3% of system energy consumption compared to benchmark
schemes.
Index Terms—Maritime network, edge computing, LEO satellite
network, computation offloading.

serves as an emerging computing paradigm [4]. Deploying edge
servers on LEO satellites, rich computing capacity is gathered

at satellite edge. As a complement to the terrestrial network,
the LEO satellite provides high-quality computing services for
maritime IoT devices. Therefore, maritime IoT devices can
offload tasks to LEO satellite for processing, alleviating the
computational and energy burden.
Partial offloading is recognized in MEC as a computational
paradigm. The communication and computing resources of the
LEO satellites are still limited, making it impractical to offload
all tasks to the LEO satellites for processing. On the other hand,
MWDs offload massive task size, generates additional trans-
mission energy and latency. LEO satellites and OBS can utilize
solar energy as an energy supply, but communication and daily
operation consume a large amount of energy. Therefore, it is
crucial to reduce unnecessary energy waste through energy con-
sumption optimization to improve the life cycle and operational
efficiency of LEO satellites and OBS. Thus, partial offloading is
more meaningful in reducing system energy consumption while
satisfying latency constraints.
A. Related Works
MEC technology provides a promising solution for computa-
tion offloading. Qin et al. [5] investigated the perceptual compu-
tation offloading scheme, which considered the stochastic nature
of the UAV task generation sequence and server load to optimize
offloading strategy and resource assignment. Chen et al. [6]
researched task offloading in distributed networks, where device
associations, offloading decisions, and trajectories are optimized
to maximize the quality of experience. Liu et al. [7] proposed a
multivariate nonlinear coupled latency minimization problem
to reduce latency by optimizing cache resource assignment.
Gao et al. [8] optimized offloading strategy for devices using
attention-weighted graph recurrent networks, which improved
the generalization ability of offloading scheme. Pham et al. [9]
studied a vehicle assisted computing system, where devices
offload partial task to servers or nearby vehicles for maximizing
offloading utility of mobile devices. Shen et al. [10] investigated
a UAV-assisted computing system, where UAVs can process
tasks for IoT devices to minimize energy consumption. Jiang
et al. [11] explored network slicing, resource allocation, and
introducing a two-level slicing model to maximize successful
processing rate.
The research on satellite edge computing has yielded many
significant achievements. Lakew et al. [12] studied a LEO-
enabled network model where multiple LEO satellites provide
computing services to resource-constrained energy harvesting
UAVs. Nguyen et al. [13] investigated a hybrid computing
system, which optimizes offloading decision and resource op-
timization to reduce weighted computing energy consumption.
Wang et al. [14] proposed a computation offloading scheme by
optimizing offloading selection and resource allocation to mini-
mize weighted energy consumption. Cheng et al. [15] proposed
a satellite dynamic offloading strategy to minimize the overall
mission completion time by optimizing task offloading and
resource allocation. Gao et al. [16] studied the multi-user compu-
tation offloading problem, which minimizes the system overhead
by optimizing offloading strategy and transmission power. Ding
et al. [17] proposed the satellite-terrestrial assisted multi-tier
computing network to reduce computing energy consumption.
Zhang et al. [18] proposed a distributed offloading scheme that
employs a counterfactual multi-agent policy gradient scheme
to minimize latency. Zhang et al. [19] studied task scheduling
problem in SAGIN, in which IoT devices offload computing
tasks to UAVs. The offloading strategy is optimized to minimize
the energy consumption of UAVs. Zhou et al. [20] designed
a distributed algorithm for efficiently solving the computation
offloading problem in satellite networks. Tang et al. [21] inves-
tigated a LEO satellite-supported edge system, in which user
association and computing resource are jointly optimized to
reduce energy consumption.
To efficiently perform computing tasks for MWDs, many
studies have explored computation offloading schemes in mar-
itime communication networks. Dai et al. [22] presented a off-
shore and airborne computing scheme, which minimizes latency
by optimizing offloading decisions and computing resource al-
location. Dai et al. [23] proposed a maritime offloading scheme,
where UAVs and surface sink nodes provide computing services
for MWD. Li et al. [24] studied a maritime computation offload-
ing by optimizing position and transmission power of unmanned
surface vehicles (USVs) to reduce energy consumption. Dai
et al. [25] investigated a UAV-assisted computation offloading
by optimizing offloading strategy to achieve minimum energy
consumption. Dai et al. [26] proposed a UAV-assisted offloading
scheme with the goal of increasing the system benefits of mar-
itime edge computing networks. Xu et al. [27] proposed a UAV-
based marine offloading scheme to minimize overall latency by
optimizing user scheduling and UAV trajectories, and resource
allocation. Zeng et al. [28] proposed a USV computation offload-
ing scheme and a joint task and resource allocation scheme to
minimize energy consumption of USVs. Lyu et al. [29] studied
a marine task offloading problem by introducing a coalitional
game method to achieve a Nash equilibrium in order to minimize
the system overhead.
In summary, energy consumption is typically a critical crite-
rion for performance evaluation in SEC. However, the impor-
tance of LEO satellites for maritime communication and com-
putation has been neglected in the past studies on computation
offloading for maritime networks. Therefore, we consider the
characteristics of LEO satellite and OBS and design a maritime
computation scheme based on OBS and LEO satellite to provide
services for MWDs. Existing works on computation offloading
are summarized in Table I .
B. Our Contributions
We introduce LEO satellite and an OBS into maritime edge
computing network, which jointly provide communication and
computing services for MWDs. Considering the strict latency
constraints of tasks, we present a LEO satellite and OBS-assisted
partial offloading scheme. MWDs split computing task into
three parts, which are processed in local, LEO satellite, and
OBS, respectively. Eventually, we optimize association variable,
task partitioning, transmission power, and computing resource
allocation to minimize system energy consumption. The main
contributions of the paper are as follows.

V. CONCLUSION
This paper designs a maritime edge computing system which
aims to provide communication and computing services for
MWDs. We formulate a non-convex energy consumption mini-
mization problem. Specifically, to solve the MINLP problem, we
decompose original problem into four subproblems and design
algorithms to solve the corresponding subproblems. First, for the
associated variable subproblem, we use slack variable method to
transform the subproblem into a convex problem for solving. We
solve joint transmission power optimization of MWDs and LEO
satellites subproblem using quadratic transformation method.
Then, the upper and lower bounds of offloading task size are
obtained by deducing constraints, which are utilized for solving
task partitioning subproblem. We solve joint computing resource
optimization of LEO satellites and OBS subproblem using La-
grangian dual method and coordinate transformation method to
obtain computing resource allocation. Thereafter, we design an
iterative algorithm to jointly optimize the association variable,
transmission power, task partitioning and computing resource
allocation to obtain optimal variables to minimize system energy
consumption. Finally, the performance of the proposed scheme
in multiple environments is verified by simulation results. In the
future, we will explore the complexity of the proposed scheme,
challenges, and the key factors (e.g., spectrum resources) for
scaling and deploying the scheme in real-world scenarios. In
addition, we will study satellite-marine computing schemes in
dynamic scenarios and consider designing UAV-assisted mar-
itime edge computing systems.
